openQuestions: Trim kind "version" (not in types.ts) is also used in other card files under src/data/model-cards/ (e.g. tatra, toyota); fixed only for vauxhall here. A repo-wide normalisation to "technical-version" is suggested.

Many generations still have facelift null (unreviewed): Vectra B (1999), Vectra C (2005), Omega B (1999), Corsa C (2003), Corsa D (2010/11), Astra G, Astra J (2012), Agila A, Tigra, Combo C/D, Vivaro A/B, Movano B (Master 2019 facelift did/did not carry over). Not verified in this pass.

Monterey received a further facelift in 1998 per Wikipedia; the card generation ends in 1998, so it was not added. Trims from 1991/1992 are Isuzu Trooper dates and were left as-is pending a UK-specific source.
Movano C added without photo or trims; exact diesel displacement (2.2 Multijet) not in the sources read, left null.

Belmont/Viceroy/Senator trims were taken from auto-data pages that carry Opel-era start years; clamped to the Vauxhall generation start. Senator A2 3.0 E trim (132 kW) may correspond to the Vauxhall 3.0i; name left unchanged.

Not proposed as missing (LCVs unlikely to be met by Czech buyers): Vauxhall Arena (Renault Trafic, 1997–2001), Brava (Isuzu pickup), Rascal (Suzuki Carry), Midi (Bedford Midi). Confirm whether LCV-only lines belong in the auto section.
summary: Vauxhall card checked against Wikipedia (oldid), press/trade sources and auto-data: fixed invalid trim kind on all trims, wrong body types on Movano/Combo B/Agila A trims, Opel-era trim start years on Belmont/Viceroy/Senator, added 9 missing facelifts (incl. Astra L 2026, Mokka B 2024, Combo E/Vivaro C 2023) and the missing Movano C (2021–) generation. models-auto lacks 30 card lines and carries 15 generation-level entries plus a duplicate "12".
